themes.name: Critical Thinking Development through AI Integration
themes.definition: The integration of Generative AI tools with pedagogical strategies to foster critical analysis, evaluation, and synthesis of information. This theme encompasses guided prompt-building, metacognitive scaffolding, and critique of AI-generated outputs to enhance analytical reasoning.
evidence: [Crudele2025] 'Argumentative skills...fostering critical thinking (CT)...guided prompt-building techniques...support critical engagement with intelligent agents'
[Drushlyak2025] 'ChatGPT...an essential training tool...develop pre-service teachers' critical thinking...proved effective'
[Nusivera2025] 'students' interaction with AI Chat-GPT produces a dialogue that encourages students to analyze, evaluate, and synthesize information, which is a major component in CT skills'

themes.name: Prompt Literacy and Human-AI Collaboration
themes.definition: The ability to construct effective queries for AI tools and engage in iterative dialogue with generative AI. This includes explicit instruction on prompt design and balancing AI assistance with human oversight.
evidence: [Umer2025] 'challenges included the need for precise prompt construction...faculty stressed the need for critical evaluation of LLM outputs'
[Crudele2025] 'guided prompt-building techniques that align with AI literacy...students practiced creating effective prompts to better interact with AI'
[Alves2025] 'half of the students demonstrated...judgment in selecting from multiple GPT-generated solutions'

themes.name: Ethical and Epistemic Challenges in AI Usage
themes.definition: Concerns about AI-generated inaccuracies, academic integrity, and over-reliance on technology. Includes strategies to balance automation with critical evaluation of AI outputs.
evidence: [Ganjoo2024] 'students noted concerns about academic integrity and lack of citations in GAI responses...68.8% agreed GAI should require instructor authorization'
[Zhang2025e] 'students' agreement with CodeTutor's suggestions decreased...growing preference for human teaching assistants'
[Haidar2025] 'metacognitive regulation is a more meaningful predictor of writing skills than knowledge'

themes.name: Multimodal and Interactive AI Pedagogies
themes.definition: Pedagogical approaches combining AI tools with multimodal content (text, images, simulations) to enhance engagement and creative exploration. Includes flipped classrooms, design thinking, and visual diagnostic training.
evidence: [Lyu2026] 'media literacy training strengthened access, analysis, and evaluation of AI-generated images...transformed student communication'
[Chen2025e] 'Midjourney vs Pinterest...generative AI tools reduced strategic evaluations in creative exploration'
[Bani-Hamad2024] 'Fermi Problem-Based Learning with AI...improved science students' creative and critical thinking'

themes.name: AI-Enhanced Self-Regulated Learning
themes.definition: AI tools supporting autonomous learning processes including goal-setting, reflection, and adaptive strategies. Focuses on metacognitive awareness and strategic adjustments during learning tasks.
evidence: [Chen2025e] 'traditional tools required more frequent reflections on the design process and higher metacognitive behavior'
[YldzDurak2025] 'GenAI as metacognitive scaffolding...significantly increased metacognitive strategy use in flipped classrooms'
[Haidar2025] 'metacognitive prompts by GenAI in collaborative writing...activated metacognitive processes and strategy use'

data.meta_observations: The overwhelming focus on 'Critical Thinking Development' across 22/25 articles suggests this is a central concern in AI-integrated education. However, the lack of quantitative data limits verification of claimed impacts. Multiple abstracts show tension between AI's efficiency benefits and risks of cognitive dependence. 'Prompt literacy' emerges as a distinct competence separate from general AI literacy.
data.grounding_notes: All themes strictly derive from verbatim text in abstracts. High-confidence themes (1-3) appear in multiple disciplines (STEM, humanities, medical education) with consistent terminology. Lower-frequency themes (4-5) may be underreported due to quality issues in abstracts (missing methods/results in 14/25 entries).
